draft.title: Tests for congruent triangles
card: Congruent triangles are the same shape and size. Every side and angle in one matches a side and angle in the other.
You do not need to check all six parts. Three matching parts can be enough if they fit one of the tests.
SSS: all three sides match. SAS: two sides match and the angle between them matches.
AAS: two angles and a side match, with the side in the same place in both. RHS: a right angle, the hypotenuse and one other side match.
draft.remember: Three matching parts that fit SSS, SAS, AAS or RHS prove two triangles congruent.

a.q: Triangle ABC has sides 5 cm, 7 cm and 9 cm. Triangle PQR has sides 9 cm, 5 cm and 7 cm. Which test shows they are congruent?
a.why: All three pairs of sides match, so the test is SSS. SAS is wrong because no angle is given.
a.clue: Count how many sides are known and whether any angles are given.

b.q: Two triangles each have sides of 6 cm and 8 cm. In both, the angle between those two sides is 40°. Are the triangles congruent?
opts: No, three matching parts are not enough
b.why: Two sides and the angle between them match, so the triangles are congruent by SAS. SSS does not apply because the third sides are not given as equal. Three matching parts are enough when they fit a test.
b.clue: Where does the angle sit compared with the two sides?
